speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Related amendments will also be made to the Consumer Protection (Trade Descriptions and Safety Requirements) Act 1975 and the Weights and Measures Act 1975.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Since taking over the fair-trading function from then-SPRING Singapore in 2018, CCCS has deepened its expertise and established itself as one of the key pillars underpinning our consumer protection ecosystem today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: It works closely with relevant Government agencies and the Consumers Association of Singapore to promote consumer education and awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: CCCS also takes action against unfair practices under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act 2003 (or CPFTA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: It plays an important role in safeguarding consumer interests, ensuring they can transact with businesses with peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Product safety and the accurate measurement of products are vital in protecting consumer interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Today, product safety and legal metrology functions are administered by Enterprise Singapore’s Consumer Product Safety Office (CPSO), and the Weights and Measures Office (WMO), respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: This results in the consumer protection functions to reside across two agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Such a move would reinforce the mandate of CCCS’ to protect consumers by enhancing its oversight of consumer protection issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: The Bill will transfer the following functions from Enterprise Singapore to CCCS, namely: One, promoting the supply of safe consumer goods among suppliers in Singapore and educating consumers on safety information of the goods they buy and legal metrology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Two, preventing the supply of unsafe consumer goods in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Three, the administration and enforcement of the Weights and Measures Act, including the regulation of weighing and measuring instruments used for trade, the provision of relevant information relating to quantity in the supply of goods, and enforcement actions against suppliers whose goods are short-weighted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Four, representing Singapore internationally and advising Government agencies and consumer protection organisations on promoting and enforcing the supply of safe consumer goods in Singapore, including providing relevant safety information about consumer goods and legal metrology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: The Bill will also empower CCCS to designate or recognise persons who perform conformity assessment, testing or certification related to product safety of consumer goods, to regulate such persons, or to carry out the conformity assessment or testing itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: CCCS will also be empowered to administer and enforce certain regulations under Consumer Protection (Trade Descriptions and Safety Requirements) Act, including regulations relating to the supply of safe consumer goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: This further complements the existing enforcement functions against unfair practices under the CPFTA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: If passed, all assets, liabilities and records of the CPSO and WMO in Enterprise Singapore will be transferred to CCCS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: Enterprise Singapore and CCCS will ensure smooth continuity of operations and provide support to the public and industry stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for t
text: We will engage with all relevant stakeholders in the lead-up to the transfer.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This move will reshape the regulatory landscape for businesses and consumers alike.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: At the heart of this Bill lies a fundamental question: how do we strike the right balance between protecting consumers and ensuring that businesses, especially small ones, can continue to thrive?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us be clear: consumer protection is not just about making sure products are safe.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is about trust – trust that when you buy something, it works as promised; trust that businesses play fair; trust that when things go wrong, the system will act, quickly and decisively.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: CASE has and continues to work closely with CCCS on many issues relating to consumer protection.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: CASE therefore supports the proposed amendments as they will effectively consolidate the enforcement of consumer protection issues under CCCS.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Over the years, CASE has been conducting its own product safety testing.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: With this amendment, I foresee that CASE will work even more closely with CCCS to identify issues related to product safety and misleading product claims, to better protect consumers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, I have some questions and suggestions regarding this Bill.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Seven years later, I would like to ask if this was achieved and how does the Ministry intend to ensure that we do not lose this competitive advantage once the product safety and legal metrology functions are transferred to CCCS? ⁠How will stakeholders, such as the businesses, Conformity Assessment Bodies and registered suppliers of Controlled Goods, be impacted by this transfer of functions?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will there be any impact on CCCS and Enterprise Singapore officers as a result of the transfer?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As Members of this House would be aware, I have been calling for unit pricing since 2022, to tackle the phenomenon of shrinkflation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I therefore, welcome the trial, which will see supermarket operators display unit pricing for daily essentials, such as rice, meat, eggs, cooking oils, fruits and vegetables.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that the trial will provide useful insights that could lead to a nationwide implementation of unit pricing soon.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: CASE has been studying issues related to unit pricing rollout in other key jurisdictions and I am keenly aware of some of the operational challenges faced overseas.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Cooking oil is supplied in Singapore, both in terms of volume, meaning in litres; and also in weight, meaning in kilogrammes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One of the challenges of trying to unit price cooking oil will be if a retailer tries to convert all varieties of cooking oil into a standardised unit of measure.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Different oils have different densities and the formula will differ across, for example, vegetable oil, sesame oil and avocado oil.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I would, therefore, like to suggest for CCCS to have powers under the Weights and Measures Act or under CPFTA, to make decisions on the exact conversion formula to be used, if a complaint is made to the agency regarding such matters.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In 2022, I spoke about the need to significantly shorten the time taken by CCCS to obtain an injunction order to stop errant businesses from perpetuating their unfair business practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I urge the Government to reconsider my proposals for CCCS to have the ability to impose financial penalties on errant businesses without having to first obtain an injunction order from the Courts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Additionally, even if CCCS successfully obtains an injunction order against an errant business, affected consumers are still required to separately file their cases at the Small Claims Tribunals to seek compensation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that CCCS could be provided powers to issue Directions to businesses to compensate consumers, in cases where the agency has been awarded an injunction order by the Courts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As the number of complaints handled by CASE continues to rise on a yearly basis, I urge the Government to provide CCCS with greater enforcement powers so that we can have a robust consumer protection regime.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As we do so, we should have an eye on future consumer protection issues, including potential disputes pertaining to the roll-out of unit pricing and to provide CCCS with greater administrative and enforcement powers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This will enhance CCCS' oversight of consumer protection issues and relevant regulations and strengthen its ability to engage both consumers and businesses on consumer protection matters.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I will, first, address the Members' specific questions about the transfer of functions, before addressing the broader points raised by both Members on our consumer protection regime.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: President of CASE, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about CCCS' ability to administer the product safety and legal metrology regimes following the transfer.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: First, such enforcement functions are not new to CCCS.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As I had shared earlier, during the start of the reading, CCCS has developed expertise as well as experience as a regulatory authority on unfair trading practices since 2018.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Taking over these additional consumer protection functions on product safety and legal metrology is complementary and, in fact, synergistic to its existing functions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: All public officers in CPSO and WMO will move over accordingly to ensure continuity and enhance cross-sharing of expertise and there will be no impact to other officers in either Enterprise Singapore or CCCS.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As there will be no change to the capabilities and processes of CPSO and WMO, industry stakeholders as well as the members of the public can continue to access the services and the resources that are provided by CPSO as well as WMO during the transfer.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: More details on the new contact touchpoints following the transfer will certainly be provided to involve stakeholders soon.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These steps will set CCCS' ability to administer the product safety and legal metrology regimes from the get-go following the transfer.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I will now address the two Members' questions on our broader approach towards consumer protection.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As shared in my speech at the Ministry of Trade and Industry's Committee of Supply debate, in fact, just last month, the Government is certainly very mindful that for markets to function properly, consumers' trust in merchants and markets must be upheld.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To do so, we must ensure that the regulatory system is fair and transparent to protect consumers while ensuring that the businesses can operate efficiently and are on the same level playing field.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I fully agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng on the importance of maintaining this balance and I also agree with Mr Melvin Yong on the need to ensure that our regulations remain robust and effective.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: First, we believe that regulations should be clear, transparent and fit-for-purpose without creating excessive burden.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We also take a practical approach to consumer protection regulations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, our product safety regime adopts a risk-based approach where stricter regulations, including registration and testing, apply only to a defined list of higher-risk household appliances, such as refrigerators and cooking appliances.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For most of general consumer goods, for example, sports equipment and furniture, we then take a more self-regulatory approach, requiring the products to adhere to applicable international as well as local safety standards.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We also provide guidelines and resources to help businesses better understand and comply with our regulations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, CPSO and WMO send compliance advisories to our businesses, including SMEs, through the trade associations and also e-commerce platforms.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Because when everyone understands the rules, it then creates a fairer marketplace where businesses can focus on what they do best and provide safe and high-quality products for our consumers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Consumer education is also critical in ensuring consumers are aware of product characteristics and are able to make informed decisions when purchasing and also using the products.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, CPSO communicates educational information and safety tips via its website to educate and also alert the consumers of products that are at higher risk of safety breaches.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Second, we proactively consult and also engage industry stakeholders, including SMEs, as well as other partners, when reviewing our regulations, to ensure that we incorporate the perspectives of the private sector and consider the latest developments.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For instance, CPSO has set up an Advisory Committee comprising industry experts, academics and Government representatives to provide objective and independent advice on whether certain household appliances should be added to or should be removed from the list of controlled goods.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As both Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Yip Hon Weng have pointed out, consumer markets are constantly evolving and becoming more diverse, from digital goods and online marketplaces to groceries and daily essentials.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Government is certainly cognisant of these developments and is certainly working with the industry to closely monitoring all the developments.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have already started our work to actively consult the industries as part of a more fundamental review of our consumer protection regime.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Panel is co-chaired by Mr Melvin Yong and retired judicial commissioner Ms Foo Tuat Yien.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Panel will develop recommendations to drive consumer empowerment, raise industry standards and strengthen regulatory levers, where appropriate.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Panel held its kick-off meeting last week and we certainly look forward to receiving and studying the Panel's recommendations in time to come.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These key elements of balance, trust and partnership underpin the Government's approach to consumer protection and we will certainly continue to refine and strengthen our approach.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications for Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling?
